fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # 20 years after Kofi Annan, Africa is back in the race to produce its third UN Secretary-General. Twenty years after Ghana's Kofi Annan stepped down as Secretary-General of the United Nations, Africa is once again in contention to lead the world's largest multilateral organization. * Senegal's former president Macky Sall is Africa's only declared candidate in the race to become the next UN Secretary-General. * If selected, Sall would be the first African to lead the UN since Kofi Annan's tenure ended in 2006, breaking a two-decade absence of African leadership. Senegal's former president, Macky Sall, is hoping to become the third African to occupy the UN's highest office. If ultimately selected by the Security Council and approved by the UN General Assembly, Sall would become the first African Secretary-General since Kofi Annan left office in 2006, ending a two-decade absence of African leadership at the helm of the global body.
